classification.difficultyReason: Read the labelled asymptotes to obtain b and c, then select the numerator sign from branch orientation; the equation form and interpretation method are supplied.

content.prompt: Determine the equation of these hyperbolas in the form $y=\pm\dfrac{1}{x-b}+c$.

spec.description: Positive reciprocal branches with labelled dashed asymptotes; no grid or ticks. The source origin letter is omitted under house graph conventions.
spec.mathematics: y=1/(x-2)-1; vertical asymptote x=2; horizontal asymptote y=-1.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph and its asymptote labels are permanent givens; the equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The asymptotes are $x=2$ and $y=-1$, so $b=2$ and $c=-1$. The branches are top right and bottom left relative to the asymptotes, so the numerator is positive.
$$y=\frac{1}{x-2}-1$$
